literal: By an action, an action having made, accomplishing (is) wet cheek by an elephant an elephant having bound like.
translation: Accomplishing one task through another is like using a rutting elephant to capture another wild elephant.
modern: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்யும்போதே அதைப் பயன்படுத்தி மற்றொரு செயலையும் முடித்துக்கொள்வது, மதநீர் ஒழுகும் ஒரு யானையை வைத்து மற்றொரு யானையைப் பிடிப்பதைப் போன்றதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet explains the strategy of achieving multiple goals efficiently. It compares the process of using one ongoing action to accomplish another to the traditional method of capturing wild elephants. Just as a trained elephant with wet cheeks (indicating rut or maturity) is used to lure and bind a wild elephant, a wise person uses the momentum and resources of one task to complete another. The words 'வினையான் வினை' (action by action) and 'யானையால் யானை' (elephant by elephant) create a strong parallel that emphasizes leveraging existing efforts.
